BUDGET REASONING (the load-bearing decision): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. val=ALL 214 L277 slices is MANDATORY (protocol; do NOT reduce). 18-min outer wall (naf_outer_wall_s=1080, inside the 20-min compute budget, leaving headroom for the figure+IO before the 30-min sbatch kill) / 214 scenes = naf_per_scene_s=5.0 s/scene. Mayo is 512x512 images at 2304 views x 736 channels, so each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + a 2304-view fan-beam forward-project + backward = EXPENSIVE; 5 s/scene buys only a handful of steps (a NeRF-style fit wants hundreds-to-thousands). naf_n_iter=3000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor -- each scene runs as many steps as fit in 5 s. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT -- solver_plan.md flags NAF/R2G hr~0 on dense-view; the discarded boundary-slice run hinted naf 0.911 < LD-FBP ~0.81-cal baseline, a behavior hint only) AND it is BUDGET-STARVED on the 214-slice protocol (5 s/scene = far too few per-scene Adam steps for a NeRF-style convergence). Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the LD-FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint under the corrected metric -- a real finding (do NOT reduce val_n below 214 to make NAF look better). iter-2+ will tune ONE knob (per-scene step budget vs MLP capacity vs lr) but NAF cannot escape its structural ceiling on this dense substrate within a 20-min/214-scene budget.

advice_for_others: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=4, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, naf). SIX-BOX. (1) iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.4729, hr 0.0, PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08; elapsed 1097s; naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2; SLURM [fit] log shows each scene fit only ~85-97 Adam steps (median 91) before the 5.0s per-scene wall, and the 18-min outer wall (1080s) was hit EXACTLY at scene 214 (elapsed 1082.5s). (2) FAILURE MODE: budget-starved per-scene INR fit. A NeRF-style coordinate-MLP wants hundreds-to-thousands of Adam steps to leave its water-mu init; ~91 steps/scene leaves the MLP barely moved -> SSIM 0.4729 well below the LD-FBP baseline. This is starvation, NOT (yet) the structural floor. (3) ONE KNOB: naf_hidden 128->64 (naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). 214-SCENE 20-MIN BUDGET MATH (measured): the entire budget is the per-scene fit loop (train_n=0); total = 214 x per_scene_s = 214 x 5.0s = 1070s ~= the 1080s/18-min outer wall, hit exactly at scene 214. I CANNOT raise per_scene_s (214 x wall is already full inside the 20-min compute budget). So to buy MORE Adam steps per scene at FIXED total budget I make each step CHEAPER: per-step cost ~0.055 s/step is the fixed 2304-view fan-beam forward+backward PLUS the tunable 512^2-coord MLP forward; halving width 128->64 cuts the dominant hidden x hidden matmuls ~4x, so each 5.0s scene should fit meaningfully more steps -> more useful optimization per scene within the SAME 214 x 1080s/18-min wall. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I shrink naf_hidden 128->64, I expect SSIM to rise above 0.4729 because the cheaper MLP buys more Adam steps per scene, letting the INR move further off its water-mu init within the same per-scene wall. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.47 despite more steps, NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT), not merely starved. (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall = the governor; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap), val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

FALSIFIER: if the ~9 scenes that finish at gs_n_iter=400 score <=0.76 SSIM (no material lift over 0.738), under-fit is REFUTED and 0.738 is a per-scene structural ceiling. BUDGET MATH: 282.9 ms/step x 400 steps = 113.2 s/scene; 1080s outer wall / 113.2 = ~9/214 scenes finish (well within the 20-min train+score budget; SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced); the per-scene loop self-truncates at the 1080s wall and scores whatever completed -- exactly as iter-1. ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 400->60 (per-scene Adam steps DOWN to MAXIMIZE completed-scene COVERAGE; all other knobs held at iter-2). FAILURE MODE (the core, structural problem): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at a hard 20-min wall. Measured per-scene step cost is a clean linear function of gs_n_iter: iter-1 (n_iter=150) = 42.45 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 26/214 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335, hr=0; iter-2 (n_iter=400) = 113.0 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 10/214 (4.7% coverage), SSIM 0.736981, hr=0. Linear fit: 0.2822 s/Adam-step (offset ~0). iter-2 FALSIFIER FIRED: the hypothesis 'more Adam steps lifts per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738' is REFUTED -- 2.67x more steps (150->400) moved the average-over-214 SSIM by -0.0001 (0.7383 -> 0.7370, FLAT). So per-scene quality is NOT the lever; the average is dominated by the ~95% of scenes that NEVER complete (scored at/near their FBP init). DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION for iter-3: does COVERAGE win? At gs_n_iter=60 -> per-scene = 0.2822*60 = 16.9 s -> 1080s outer wall / 16.9 = ~64/214 scenes complete (30% coverage, ~2.5x iter-1's 26, ~6.4x iter-2's 10). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): if the average-over-214 SSIM goes UP at 64-scene coverage (vs 0.738 @ 26 scenes and 0.737 @ 10 scenes), coverage is the lever and R2-Gaussian is coverage-limited (not quality-limited) on Mayo. FALSIFIER: if average-over-214 SSIM stays ~0.74 or WORSE even at 2.5x coverage, then BOTH levers (per-scene quality AND coverage) are exhausted within the 20-min budget -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol -> file the quality-vs-coverage tradeoff as a documented NEGATIVE RESULT (no gs_n_iter both covers all 214 AND fits per-scene: covering all 214 in 1080s needs n_iter<=18 steps, which is a non-recon). BUDGET MATH: 64 scenes * 16.9 s = 1082s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/iter-2); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (26/214) -> iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-3 predicted ~0.74-0.76 if coverage helps (64/214), or ~0.74 (structural negative) if it does not.

Trajectory: the clip bump moved hr +0.072 (0.133->0.205) and dropped RMSE 8.3% by un-truncating high-mu bone -- the clamp WAS the binding constraint (iter-2 falsifier 'hr<=0.133' NOT triggered). iter-2 clip_max=0.08 is now at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] so clip is exhausted as a lever. tv_lambda has been FROZEN at the solver default 0.001 for BOTH prior iters -- never probed -- and is the highest-value untouched knob (the classical data-vs-smoothness balance). advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-1 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric): feasibility baseline, NO prior iter. Unrolled K=10 TV-GD with per-iter learnable step+lambda (20 trainable scalars), supervised-L2 vs clean truth, init from LD-FBP. SEEDED from the sibling classical tv_iterative iter-1 corner (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133): tv_step_init=0.01 (=classical tv_lr), tv_lambda_init=0.001 (=classical tv_lambda), tv_clip_max=0.05. ADDS a SHORT supervised training phase (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1) on top of the 214-slice val pass. BUDGET (HARD 20 min train+score): classical tv_iterative ran 120 GD-iters x 214 slices in 918s (~0.036 s/slice-iter, dominated by the 2304-view 512px projector pair). This variant: val = K=10 unrolled x 214 slices, val_chunk=5 -> ~80-120s. Train = 40 samples x 8 epochs x K=10 x (fwd+bwd, ~2-3x a val slice-iter) ~ 256-380s. + 214-slice FBP precompute + load ~120s. Total ~7-10 min, ~2x margin under the 1200s wall. bs=1 holds only one K-step autograd graph at a time (memory-safe on 16 GB; no OOM risk vs the hammernik bs=4 OOM). FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: (a) 214-slice TV recon x training blows the wall -> kept K, train_n, epochs conservative; (b) under-training the 20 scalars -> epochs=8 gives the learnable step/lambda schedule room to depart from the seed while still fitting. HYPOTHESIS: a LEARNED per-iter lambda schedule lands at or slightly ABOVE the classical fixed-lambda tv_iterative hr 0.133, because the supervised end-to-end fit can adapt the data-vs-TV balance per unrolled step rather than holding one fixed lambda. If it under-performs the classical baseline, the K=10 unrolled depth (vs classical 120 iters) is the limiter and iter-2 raises tv_K.

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). PRIOR: iter-1 SSIM 0.2855 / hr 0.0, elapsed 321.5s — FAR below the classical (non-trained) tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133). FAILURE MODE (diagnosed iter-1): tv_K=10 unrolled steps is FAR too shallow vs classical TV (~120 iters) -> the recon is severely under-resolved; the 20 learnable scalars cannot compensate for missing depth. ONE KNOB CHANGED: tv_K 10 -> 30 (3x deeper unroll). All else identical to iter-1 (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, lr=5e-3, val_n=214 ALL L277 slices, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00 with 10-min figure/IO headroom): iter-1 ran K=10 in 321.5s. Worst-case PURE-linear-in-K (assume all 321.5s is K-bound, fixed overhead=0): 32.15 s/K -> K=30 ~= 964s, ~20% under the 1200s wall. In reality a large slice of 321.5s is FIXED overhead (data load + 214-slice FBP precompute + per-ps probe ~60-120s), so the true K=30 cost is well under 964s. bs=1 holds only ONE K-step autograd graph at a time -> deeper K raises activation memory linearly but stays memory-safe on 16 GB (no OOM; cf. the hammernik bs=4 OOM). HYPOTHESIS: deeper unroll lifts SSIM toward the classical 0.92 band and clears baseline (hr>0), because 30 TV-GD steps resolve far more of the data-consistency + edge structure than 10 (closing the gap to classical 120 iters), and the learned per-iter step/lambda schedule adapts the balance across the deeper unroll. FALSIFIER: if SSIM/hr stay low at K=30, the limiter is NOT depth but the supervised-TV TRAINING (e.g. broken target/loss/optimisation), and iter-3 must check the training path (loss curve, learned step/lambda trajectory) rather than deepening further.

TRAINING-DIAGNOSIS iter, NOT a hyperparameter tune. PRIOR: iter-1 (K=10) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 321.5s; iter-2 (K=30) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 946s -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to every digit, comparison.png identical (289606 B). iter-2 deepened the unroll 10->30 and the result did NOT change AT ALL -> depth is FALSIFIED as the limiter. SLURM TRAINING LOG (jobs 765204 iter-1 / 765283 iter-2) shows the smoking gun: loss=0.001739 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs, and the learnable step[k]=0.01, lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init for all 8 epochs -- the 20/60 scalars receive ZERO gradient and never move. FAILURE MODE (named): the supervised TV TRAINING is structurally frozen by a SATURATED-CLAMP gradient kill. Mechanism: data_grad = back_project(Rf - sino) is the RAW unfiltered adjoint of a 2304-view Mayo sinogram (sum-scaled, NO 1/N normalization). The classical tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92) computes its gradient via AUTOGRAD on 0.5*mean(residual^2) -- a mean over 2304*736~1.7e6 elements -> per-element gradient ~1.7e6x SMALLER. tv_step_init=0.01 was inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr but the supervised path's gradient is ~1.7e6x bigger, so f - 0.01*data_grad overshoots massively -> clamp(0,0.05) saturates the WHOLE image at K=1 -> the saturated clamp has derivative 0 everywhere -> no gradient reaches log_step/log_lambda -> scalars frozen, recon a near-constant clamped blob (PSNR 1.87, RMSE 0.0403) regardless of K. baseline LD-FBP PSNR=34.08 (Wagner-grade) confirms the data/projector are fine -- only the unrolled step scale is wrong. PAIRED ENABLER (not an independent knob -- with frozen gradients lr is inert): outer lr 5e-3 -> 5e-2 so the now-NONZERO scalar gradients move meaningfully across 8 epochs over the log-parametrised step/lambda. All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, val_n=214 ALL L277, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: with the step un-saturated, training un-freezes -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and SSIM rises from 0.2855 toward (and ideally above) the LD-FBP floor (~0.81) / the classical TV ceiling (SSIM 0.92, hr 0.205); even landing near the FBP baseline clears the 0.2855 collapse and proves the harness is repairable. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.286 (clamp still saturates) OR the scalars still don't move, the supervised-TV harness is STRUCTURALLY BROKEN on Mayo's 2304-view scale via the shared solver's unnormalized-adjoint step (which is FORBIDDEN to edit per the no-shared-module rule) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is not viable on real Mayo LDCT under the config-only contract) and STOP iterating this solver. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score): identical compute to iter-2 (K=30, same train/val sizes) -> ~946s, ~250s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted iter trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 either >0.81 (training un-froze, harness repaired) OR ~0.286 (structural -> negative result + STOP).

advice_for_others: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). RE-DIAGNOSIS from the iter-3 SLURM LOG (job 765340), which contradicts the iter-3 observation narrative: the 0.2855->0.8137 jump was NOT training un-freezing -- it is the LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH. Log facts: loss=0.000064 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs (did NOT decrease); lambda[k]=0.001 STILL PINNED at init for all 8 epochs (zero gradient); step[k] crept only 1.06e-8->1.76e-8. At tv_step_init=1e-8 the unrolled update f = f - step*(data_grad + lam*tv_grad) is scaled to ~zero, so the K=30 unroll is a near-identity map on fbp_init: pred ~= clamp(LD-FBP). That is why SSIM=0.8137 ~= the LD-FBP floor (~0.81), recon PSNR 33.60 is JUST BELOW baseline_PSNR 34.08, and hr=0.0 (the recon does not beat its own FBP). The freeze did not get fixed -- it MOVED: iter-1/2 (step=1e-2) froze via SATURATED-CLAMP (overshoot clamps the whole image, clamp derivative 0); iter-3 (step=1e-8) freezes via VANISHING-STEP (data+TV terms scaled to nothing, lam has no effect on the output so d loss/d lam ~= 0). FAILURE MODE (named): the limiter is the STEP SCALE, not depth (tv_K falsified iter-1->2) and not epochs/lr (lr=5e-2 already; scalars still don't move because the gradient to lambda is ~0 at both step extremes). The working step lives BETWEEN the two known-frozen regimes 1e-8 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-8 -> 1e-5 (the geometric midpoint sqrt(1e-8*1e-2)=1e-5 of the two frozen endpoints). At ~1e-5 the data-consistency term back_project(Rf-sino) actually moves the image OFF the FBP init across K=30 steps (so the recon depends on lambda -> non-zero gradient reaches log_lambda -> the 30 TV scalars can finally train), while staying INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin (no whole-image saturation -> the clamp derivative is not 0 -> gradient also reaches log_step). Everything else IDENTICAL to iter-3 (lr=5e-2, K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0; tv_step_init STAYS finite/non-tiny -- do NOT revert toward 1e-8). HYPOTHESIS: with the step in the active basin, training un-freezes for REAL this time -- loss DECREASES across epochs, lambda[k] DEPARTS from 0.001 and step[k] adapts, and SSIM rises ABOVE the 0.8137 FBP passthrough toward the classical TV band (SSIM 0.85-0.92, the non-trained tv_iterative sibling hits 0.92 / hr 0.205); clearing hr>0 means the trained TV recon finally beats its own LD-FBP. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.81 with lambda STILL pinned (passthrough persists, the active basin is even narrower than 1e-5) OR collapses back toward ~0.286 (1e-5 already over-saturates the clamp), then the supervised-TV harness has NO step value that both trains the scalars AND beats FBP under Mayo's 2304-view unnormalized-adjoint scale within the config-only contract (the shared solver's raw back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is FBP-bounded on real Mayo LDCT) and STOP iterating this solver; iter-5 would only bracket the step further (e.g. 3e-6 / 3e-5) before declaring the negative. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score = 1200s wall): IDENTICAL compute to iter-3 (same K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, val_n=214, val_chunk=5 -- only the init VALUE of a scalar changes, not any loop size) -> ~918s measured iter-3, ~282s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 0.8137 (FBP passthrough, hr 0) -> iter-4 either >0.84 with lambda departing init and hr>0 (training un-froze for real) OR ~0.81 with lambda still pinned (passthrough -> bracket once at iter-5 then NEGATIVE RESULT + STOP).

This is the same capacity-for-epochs trade the champion dual_domain_supervised just ran (c16->24, ep27->10). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) TRAJECTORY iter-1 ep10 c24 -> SSIM 0.885910 / hr 0.173021 in 328.96s; iter-2 ep40 c24 -> SSIM 0.914097 / hr 0.322063 in 737.72s; iter-3 ep64 c24 -> SSIM 0.924443 / hr 0.353196 in 1085.87s (CURRENT, #2 on the Mayo board). current config uswin_c=24 epochs=64. (2) LIMITER: the epochs lever is now BOTH wall-locked AND showing diminishing returns. WALL: iter-3 ep64 used 1085.87s = 90.5pct of the 1200s budget; the iter-3 note computed ep72 -> 1174s = 19.6 min (only 26s margin), so epochs cannot meaningfully rise. DIMINISHING RETURNS: hr gained +0.149 over ep10->40 (+30 ep) but only +0.031 over ep40->64 (+24 ep) -> the per-epoch hr slope is flattening, the c24 net is approaching its training-convergence basin. iter-3's OWN falsifier named this exact pivot: 'if hr plateaus ... iter-4 must raise uswin_c (24->32)'. The new lever is CAPACITY, not epochs. (3) ONE KNOB: uswin_c 24->32, epochs 64->34; ALL else held (train_n=200, val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). BUDGET-TRADE MATH (worst-case-sized, mirroring the champion's method): from the two measured c24 (epochs, elapsed_s) points (40,737.72),(64,1085.87): per_epoch_c24 = (1085.87-737.72)/(64-40) = 14.51 s/epoch; fixed_c24 (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O) = 737.72 - 40*14.51 = 157.3s (predicts ep64 = 157.3 + 64*14.51 = 1086.0s vs actual 1085.87 -> calibration exact). WORST CASE (pessimistically assume EVERYTHING incl. the FBP adjoint scales 1.778x): per_epoch_worst = 14.51*1.778 = 25.80 s/epoch; fixed_worst = 157.3*1.778 = 279.7s. advice_for_others: wu_2015_trainable-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=4, wu_n_outer=1, lr=0.01, epochs=6, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol) for wu_2015_trainable = end-to-end TRAINABLE Wu 2015 reconstruction (solver_wu_2015_trainable.py). GOAL: does Wu-trainable run on Mayo under the corrected path (staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample model.proj/model.dense_proj swap, bg_target=truth) and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min train+score budget, scoring ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override)? ARCHITECTURE NOTE: this solver trains ONLY a handful of nn.Parameter scalars (per-band log-scale x4, sigmoid slope+offset x2, per-outer soft-threshold + residual-blend) wrapped around a band-weighted aliasing-free FBP + a soft-thresholded dense-residual pass; with wu_n_outer=1 that is 4+2+1+1 = 8 trainable scalars (n_bands=4). All scalars are HARD-CLAMPED inside the solver (band_scale 0.1-3.0, blend -0.5-2.0, soft_thresh 1e-5-0.05) so the optimizer cannot run away. CONFIG: wu_n_outer=1 (the discarded boundary-slice run flagged n_outer=1 as mandatory -- behavior hint only; it also HALVES the costly 2x-dense-projector residual pass per sample, the dominant per-slice cost), wu_n_bands=4 (default), lr=1e-2 (solver default; aggressive lr is fine for ~8 scalars and converges fast), epochs=6 (8 clamped scalars settle in very few epochs at lr=1e-2 -- this is NOT a deep net that under-trains; the real risk here is the opposite structural FBP ceiling, not under-convergence), train_n=200 stratified across the 4 Wagner train patients ps-groups, val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices, batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED by per-sample-ps (each train step + each val slice swaps model.proj AND model.dense_proj to its slice ps), grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY Mayo guard: the 2304-view FBP adjoint overflows otherwise), lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0 (defer to iter-2+; the discarded run hinted weight_decay tuning around its run-best iter-11, treat as loose behavior hint only), loss_base=mse, seed=42. BUDGET REASONING: the solver has NO in-code max_train_s wall hook (cannot add one -- must not edit the solver .py), so the budget is enforced by SIZING: with wu_n_outer=1 the per-sample cost is 1 band-weighted sparse-FBP (4-band backproject) + 1 forward_project + 1 dense-FBP + 1 back_project -- heavier than DD-UNet (iter-1 418s @ep8) but LIGHTER than the unrolled k=3 itnet_v3 (iter-1 738s @ep8) because there is no per-step unrolled DC loop; at only 6 epochs over 200 train slices the dominant cost is the 214-slice val pass at chunk=1 with the dense projector. This sizes train+score comfortably under the 20-min budget (30-min SLURM wall) with room for the figure. HYPOTHESIS: if I fit Wu-trainable at n_outer=1 / lr=1e-2 / ep=6 on 200 stratified Mayo train slices, I expect a finite val_ssim that lands in/near the LD-FBP baseline band (~0.84-0.89 SSIM, hr near 0), because Wu-trainable is a tuned-FBP family (band-reweighting + ONE soft-thresholded residual pass, NO image-domain CNN denoiser) and can only recover the small headroom that band weighting + a single residual correction buys over plain FBP -- it is structurally close to FBP, unlike the dual-domain U-Net families that landed hr~0.27. The discarded boundary-slice run hinted ~0.9135 SSIM at run-best iter-11 (loose behavior hint, NOT a validated number under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric Wu-trainable baseline that iter-2+ will improve by tuning ONE knob (epochs/weight_decay first, then band/sigmoid knobs).
